validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED. This is a real, well-documented line — the 180 km trunk that exports processed gas from the Pearl Petroleum Khor Mor gas plant to Kurdistan power stations. Independent, non-GEM corroboration: nsenergybusiness ('exported through an existing 180km-long, 24in-diameter gas pipeline to the Erbil, Chemchemal and Bazian power stations'), Dana Gas ('the 180 km pipeline supplies gas to power stations in Chemchemal, Bazian and Erbil'), Crescent Petroleum ('Gas deliveries to the Erbil Power Station commenced on 1st October 2008 via the 180 km pipeline'). CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED — gas transmission trunk (main gas export line from field to power plants), correctly PipelineType=transmission, Fuel=Gas; it is not one of the GulfPub crude/NGL lines. DUPLICATE: none found. The 180 km line feeds three plants; GEM captures it as the Khor Mor->Erbil(Pirdawood) row. Roster's P6827 (Khormor-Jambur-Kirkuk, 1.05 km, 16in) is a separate short line to Kirkuk, not this pipe; no other roster row overlaps. ENDPOINTS: the sheet name 'Pirdawood PP' = Perdawd/Pirdawd, the site of the 1,500 MW Erbil Gas Power Station (Mass Group Holding) ~22 km south of Erbil, fueled from the Khormor Gas Field Station — consistent with GEM's Khor Mor start / Erbil end and StartProvince Sulaymaniyah (Khor Mor field sits in Sulaymaniyah Governorate, ~50 km SE of Kirkuk). SPECS: Length 180 km = HIGH (nsenergy + Dana Gas + Crescent + offshore-technology). Diameter 24 in = HIGH (nsenergy '24in' + intpolicydigest). Start 2008 = HIGH (Crescent '1st October 2008' + nsenergy 'October 2008'). Capacity 3.40 bcm/y is a lesser caveat (see separate object).

validity.recommendation: Verify Owner vs Operator: independent sources make the field AND pipeline operator Pearl Petroleum (Dana Gas 35% / Crescent 35% / OMV 10% / MOL 10% / RWE 10%), not the KRG. KRG 100% ownership of the pipe asset is plausible (KRG-commissioned Kurdistan Gas Project offtake infrastructure) but is not independently confirmed — confirm before treating Owner=KRG as sourced.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists Owner1 = Kurdistan Regional Government 100% (ref = danagas Arabic KRI page, which returns 200 but does not state a KRG 100% ownership of the pipeline). Independent sources: Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum both state 'the pipeline and field are operated by Pearl Petroleum Company Limited' — the consortium Dana Gas 35% / Crescent 35% / OMV 10% / MOL 10% / RWE 10%. So the operator is Pearl Petroleum; the KRG is the gas buyer/offtaker and likely commissioned the power-station pipelines, but I could not independently verify KRG as 100% owner of this specific pipe. Lesser caveat, not an existence/classification concern.

validity.recommendation: Keep Capacity=3.40 bcm/y as a historical/nameplate figure but re-source it: the cited Qamar Energy PDF SSL-fails. 3.40 bcm/y ≈ 330 MMscf/d, the pre-2025 Khor Mor plant throughput; no source states '3.4 bcm/y' verbatim so this stays a soft number. Post-KM250 (Oct 2025) field capacity is 750 MMscf/d, but that is plant capacity, not necessarily this pipe's throughput.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity 3.40 bcm/y could not be corroborated to that exact figure by any working independent source; the cited qamarenergy PDF fails on SSL. Cross-check: 330 MMscf/d (the Khor Mor plant's long-standing pre-expansion capacity, ~9.3 Mm3/d) x 365 = ~3.41 bcm/y, so 3.40 bcm/y is a defensible conversion of the historical plant/pipeline throughput rather than a fabricated number. ProposalYear=2006 is also weakly sourced (Kurdistan Gas Project HoA was 2007; Erbil power-station site works began mid-2006) — plausible but low confidence. Neither rises to an existence/classification concern.

waypoints.name: Chamchamal (district town NW of Khor Mor, on the corridor toward Erbil)

routes.corridor_desc: ~180 km line (GEM length matches the sourced pipeline length) running NW from the Khor Mor gas plant in southern Chamchamal district (Sulaymaniyah Governorate, ~50 km SE of Kirkuk) up toward Chamchamal town, then continuing NW across into Erbil Governorate to terminate at the Erbil Gas Power Station at Perdawd south of Erbil. Named endpoints are firm; the exact intermediate alignment is NOT publicly mapped, so the corridor is bounded loosely by the two endpoints. Note the same trunk network also feeds the Chemchemal and Bazian power stations via branches (Bazian lies E toward Sulaymaniyah, so those branches are off the Erbil corridor and are not part of this row). Straight-line endpoint distance is ~125-130 km; the 180 km figure reflects routing/branching.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from independent sources: Dana Gas/Crescent confirm the 180 km pipeline runs from Khor Mor to the Erbil Power Station; 'Pirdawood'=Perdawd is the Erbil Gas Power Station site ~22 km S of Erbil. Start coordinate is the Khor Mor field/plant (35°8'N, 44°49'E from field-location search, near Qadir Karam) — approximate but tied to the named plant. End coordinate is the Erbil Gas Power Station at Perdawd (from power-station location search) — approximate, tied to the named facility. Chamchamal waypoint is a defensible on-corridor town, not a confirmed pipeline point. No coordinates were invented; every point maps to a named place. Exact route alignment not public → medium at best.
